newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean teachers end strike after wage pact.
newsitem.headline: Chilean teachers end strike after wage pact.

text.p: Chilean teachers on Monday ended a two-week strike that paralysed public schools after reaching a midnight wage agreement with the government.
The strike kept millions of children at home at a time when President Eduardo Frei, currently on an official visit to Britain, was calling education his top priority.
Teachers and students returned to classrooms after the agreement was reached after talks over the weekend.
The government agreed to add $73 million to funds budgeted for teachers' salaries next year and starting pay for a teacher will increase to $450 a month from $380.

Frei, before leaving for London on Saturday, stepped up pressure for a deal after accusing teachers' union leaders of being intransigent and contributing to poverty and backwardness. The strike became an embarrassment for Frei as better schools have been his government's stated top priority.
Despite strong economic growth and rising real wages for Chilean workers, Frei has faced periodic strikes by public employees. Doctors, bus drivers and copper miners have staged walkouts this year.
